жалко.gloss: feel sorry for; it's a pity

meanings.en: feel sorry for; it's a pity
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I just feel sorry for him.

examples.text: Что за глупость? Эдик, мне его просто жалко.
examples.trans: What nonsense is that? Edik, I just feel sorry for him.
Edik, I just feel sorry for him.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'sound, volume' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Turn up the volume on the television, please.

examples.text: Не дышать, я хочу слышать каждый тихий звук.
examples.trans: Do not breathe, I want to hear every quiet sound.
Look, it is a pity there is no sound.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just once.
Say it once more.
What do you mean, once?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take offence', paired with 'обижаться'.

examples.trans: She's offended.
Don't be offended!
She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'решить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to allow, to permit', paired with 'разрешать'.

examples.trans: May I come in?
Mum let me.
May we come in? Good day, sir.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on', paired with 'проследить'.

examples.trans: Are you watching us?
Keep an eye on the child.
What, are you watching us?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: That's no problem at all.
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'have'.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.
Nina, have a heart!

examples.text: Моя мама имела право на квартиру. Она пенсионерка.
examples.trans: My mother had a right to the flat. She is a pensioner.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('right').

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

examples.text: Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Please put your right foot on the bed.

examples.text: Я тебя обманул, и ты был прав. Теперь всё изменилось, Самсон.
examples.trans: I tricked you, and you were right. Now everything has changed, Samson.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'right; law' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She had a right to the flat.
You have no right!

examples.text: Моя мама имела право на квартиру. Она пенсионерка.
examples.trans: My mother had a right to the flat. She is a pensioner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cream, custard' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кондитер взбил нежный крем для торта.
examples.trans: The pastry chef whipped delicate cream for the cake.

examples.text: Сколько ложек коньяка добавить в крем?
examples.trans: How many spoonfuls of cognac to add to the cream?
Louis, I finished whipping the cream.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'взять'.

examples.trans: I'm not taking the knife.
Chef, I didn't take it.
We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pancake, blin' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And I thought of pancakes.

examples.text: Тогда положите мне ещё парочку блинов!
examples.trans: Then serve me a couple more pancakes!

examples.text: Большое спасибо вам за вкусные блины.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the delicious pancakes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.

examples.trans: How much does it cost?
The console costs five thousand.
And how much does the console cost?

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.en: even if, at least (with бы); although
meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even if, at least (with бы); although', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.
Have at least some tea.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.
Don't laugh at me.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'let', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.
Let him say it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.trans: Because I'm not a thief.

examples.text: Я устал, потому что много работал.
examples.trans: I'm tired because I worked a lot.
I'm at home because I'm ill.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm, quiet').

examples.trans: Good night!
He's a very calm person.

examples.text: Это ваша самоуверенность промелькнула. Спокойной ночи!
examples.trans: That was your overconfidence flashing by. Good night!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'night' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Good night!
At night I sleep.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'by the way; handy', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.
Your call is very well-timed.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('lower, bottom').

examples.trans: Bottom shelf.

examples.text: Ладно, положи её тихо на нижнюю полку.
examples.trans: Fine, put her quietly on the bottom shelf.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'linen, laundry; underwear' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У него даже постельного белья нет.
examples.trans: He doesn't even have bed linen.
Clean linen is in the wardrobe.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, вы со всей квартиры бельё принесли! У меня уже спина болит.
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you brought laundry from the whole flat! My back is hurting already.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'выкнуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get used to'.

related.gloss: to to get used to (prefixed perfective)
not to to get used to (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Я ещё не привык к Москве.
examples.trans: I am not used to Moscow yet.

examples.text: Ты уже привык к жизни в Москве?
examples.trans: Have you already gotten used to life in Moscow?
I got used to working by the law.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вобода'). Common feminine noun meaning 'freedom, liberty' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right now there's freedom, cars, the sea!
He was released (came out to freedom).

examples.text: Ну выйдешь ты через десять лет, и что? А сейчас свобода, машины, море!
examples.trans: Well, you'll get out in ten years, and then what? Right now there's freedom, cars, the sea!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to snore', paired with 'захрапеть'.

examples.trans: He snores loudly.

examples.text: Он ночью страшно и громко храпит!
examples.trans: At night he snores terribly and loudly!
